title: 10 Best Looka Alternatives in 2026
summary: Looka alternatives compared on who owns the logo and what vector files cost: Turbologo, 99designs, Brandmark, Wixel, Canva and more, priced November 2026.
body_markdown:
Key takeaways:


- Looka doesn't remove icons from its database after you buy, and five of the nine alternatives after ours publish a similar warning and sell no exclusive license: Wixel, LogoAI, LOGO.com, Canva and Shopify Logo Maker.
- Among those nine, Turbologo and 99designs state exclusive rights or full copyright by default (though Turbologo's Terms say similar AI designs may exist for other users), Design.com sells an Exclusive License, typically $145 once, and Brandmark publishes nothing on exclusivity.
- Wixel lets you download an SVG for free, and Brandmark's $35 one-time plan includes vector files for about half the price of Looka's $72 Premium package.
- For logos, our only designer plan with a list price, All-in-One, comes to at least $3,419 a month by our math, billed monthly with the Platform Fee, so it suits a team that needs a full identity, not a $72 mark.


Looka alternatives are worth a look once you read the fine print on who owns your logo. Looka is quick and cheap, with vector files for $72 once, but its help center says the icon in your logo stays in its database after you buy.


So we asked every option two questions: is the logo exclusive to you, and what does the cheapest route to vector files cost? We read each price on the vendor's own page on November 13, 2026.


[Awesomic](https://www.awesomic.com/) is first because it's our product, though it's also the priciest route here by far. The other nine are grouped by what each vendor's docs say about exclusivity: exclusive by default, sold as an upgrade, not published, then shared or not guaranteed. Within a group, the cheapest published route to vector files goes first, and a tool with no vector file goes last.


## Why people look past Looka


Looka, the Toronto company once called Logojoy, sells an AI logo maker, a Brand Kit of branded templates and an AI website. Designing is free and you pay to download, which is where the friction starts.


### The icon stays in Looka's library


Looka gives you "full copyright of your logo as a whole, but not the individual elements (e.g. symbols)". Its help article on copyright explains why: "We acquire our icons and fonts from a database, so unfortunately, we're currently unable to guarantee the copyright of the individual elements, nor do we remove them from our database after purchasing."


So the symbol at the center of your mark can turn up in another company's logo. Looka's Terms add that some symbols come from The Noun Project and that you use them "AT YOUR OWN RISK".


### Vector files start at $72


The $35 Basic package is a single PNG, 1000 by 1000 pixels, on a colored background. For PNG, EPS, SVG and PDF files in four color versions, including transparent ones, you need the $72 Premium package, a one-time purchase with unlimited changes afterward. You can change everything except the company name.


### The Brand Kit renews every year


The Brand Kit costs $96 a year, Brand Kit Web $129 a year for a published site, and the ecommerce version $299 a year, with a custom domain extra. Each renews automatically, Looka's Terms ask you to cancel at least ten business days before the period ends, and the 7-day refund window closes once you download a design file. A monthly Brand Kit exists, but Looka doesn't publish its price.


To compare kits before leaving, our roundup of[branding tools for startups](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/best-branding-tools-for-startups) puts Looka's Brand Kit beside others.


### Brand Kit templates arrive as PDFs


Looka's help center says Brand Kit files "download in a high-res PDF format". In an[r/Entrepreneur thread](https://www.reddit.com/r/Entrepreneur/comments/1b516w8/has_anyone_use_the_looka_subscription_is_it_worth/) asking whether the subscription is worth it, a customer paying for two of them called it "a genuine tool, not a toy", but said the PDF-only templates made invoices and proposals hard to edit, so they moved those to Xero and Canva. That's one Reddit user's experience, from February 2025.


## The best Looka alternatives, compared


The last column answers the exclusivity question in each vendor's own terms, and the pricing column shows whether you pay once or subscribe and the cheapest route to vector files.

AI-agent plans start at $19/month, and expert plans start at $1,799/month.[See current plans](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


Read the last column as each vendor's promise, not a legal opinion: even a "Yes" covers only what the seller controls, so every pick below still needs the trademark check further down.

### 2. Turbologo


**Overview:** Turbologo is an AI logo maker sold as one-time packs, with an ownership promise on its pricing page: it says "Turbo transfers to you the exclusive rights to use the logo for any purpose," and its FAQ says you keep full commercial rights after your edit time is over.


The catch is a "3 month access" toggle beside the price, which limits how long you can edit and re-download, while files and rights stay yours. Turbologo's Terms say that AI-generated designs carry no guarantee of uniqueness, that similar outputs may be produced for other users, and that some icons are licensed from The Noun Project, so read "exclusive rights" as its claim, not proof nobody holds a similar symbol.


**Key features:**


- Print-ready PDF and SVG files with a transparent background on Standard.
- A 13-page brand book, business cards, letterheads and social kits on Business.
- Unlimited extra logos and re-downloads while your access lasts.


**Pricing:** Lite costs $19.99 once for one low-resolution file with no transparent version, Standard is $39.99 for 3 months of access, or $59.99 for a year, with vector files, and Business is $79.99, or $119.99 for a year. Standard and Business are shown as discounts off struck-through prices, and AI generator credits cost extra, starting at $5 for 80.


**Pros:** Vector files for $39.99 once, an exclusive-rights clause in writing, a 7-day refund guarantee that ends once you download


**Cons:** Editing stops when the access period ends, Lite is low resolution with no transparent file, struck-through "original" prices make the real cost harder to judge


**What it fixes about Looka:** Written rights to the logo for $39.99, though its Terms, like Looka's, say similar designs may exist for other users.


**Final verdict:** Pick Turbologo if you want vector files and a written exclusivity clause for under $40.


### 3. 99designs


**Overview:** 99designs, part of Vista, replaces the generator with people. You post a brief, designers submit concepts in a contest, and you pick a winner. The pricing grid ticks "Full copyright ownership" on all four contest tiers, and the logo page promises "digital and print-ready files".


The tier decides who can enter. Bronze and Silver are open to designers at every level, Gold limits entry to mid and top-level designers, and Platinum admits top-level designers only and adds a dedicated manager.


**Key features:**


- Dozens of concepts from different designers in one contest.
- A 100% money-back guarantee on contests, with terms attached.
- One-to-one projects with a single designer, priced by that designer.


**Pricing:** Contests cost $249 for Bronze with about 30 concepts, $399 for Silver, $799 for Gold and $1,050 for Platinum. Prices exclude sales tax, and one-to-one work has no list price.


**Pros:** Full copyright on every tier, human designers, a money-back guarantee on contests


**Cons:** $249 is more than three times Looka's $72 Premium package, a contest covers one project rather than ongoing work, entry-level designers can enter the two cheaper tiers


**Why it ranks as a Looka alternative:** You trade a generator's shared icons for dozens of human-made directions and full copyright, paid once.


**Final verdict:** Choose 99designs when a person-made logo you fully own is worth $249 or more, once.


### 4. Design.com


**Overview:** Design.com is a logo maker with a website builder and 50+ design tools and templates, sold by subscription apart from a few free template logos. Its FAQ says "our packages are based on a monthly or annual subscription" and suggests subscribing for a month and canceling, after which you keep your license and design files.


Exclusivity is where it differs from Looka. Every package includes a standard license that's non-exclusive, so other customers can buy the same logo. An Exclusive License grants full intellectual property rights and removes the logo from the store. Its typical cost is $15 a month, $60 a year or $145 once, and not every logo has one.


**Key features:**


- EPS, SVG, PDF, PNG and JPG files, with a transparent background option.
- An editor for unlimited variations of your one logo.
- A website builder, plus a link-in-bio page and digital business card on Premium.


**Pricing:** The FAQ lists Starter at typically $25 a month and both Value and Premium at typically $34 a month. It says annual plans cost less but doesn't publish those rates.


**Pros:** Vector files on the cheapest plan, a site builder in the same subscription, a real route to exclusivity


**Cons:** No one-time purchase of the logo itself, exclusivity costs extra and isn't available on some logos, font files can't be downloaded


**Its best argument:** It's the one tool here that sells exclusivity as a separate license, and the logo leaves the store once you buy it.


**Final verdict:** Pick Design.com if you want a ready-made logo you can make exclusive for about $145 more, where that option is offered.


### 5. Brandmark


**Overview:** Brandmark is an AI logo maker priced the old way: "Buy it for life / One simple price", with "No monthly charges". You can generate unlimited logos for free and pay only to download, and the homepage says it exports SVG, PNG and PDF.


Its pricing page promises "Full copyright included" for commercial and personal use, but no page we found says whether the icon is exclusive, and its Terms are generic store wording with no clause on logo rights.


**Key features:**


- PNG and vector logo files on the $35 Basic plan.
- Free tweaks to your design on request, done by Brandmark's team.
- Up to 10 hand-crafted original concepts on Enterprise.


**Pricing:** Basic is $35 once, Designer is $95 and adds source files, brand guidelines, and business card, social and presentation designs, while Enterprise is $195 with a font download. None of the three renews.


**Pros:** Vector files for $35 once, no subscription at any tier, human tweaks at no charge


**Cons:** Exclusivity isn't addressed on any page we found, brand assets need the $95 plan, no refund policy published beyond the generic Terms


**The price argument:** SVG, PNG and PDF files for $35, about half of Looka's Premium price, with nothing to cancel.


**Final verdict:** Choose Brandmark for the cheapest one-time vector logo here, and check the icon yourself before you trademark it.


### 6. Wixel


**Overview:** Wixel is Wix's newer AI design platform, now its main logo maker, and it gives away the vector file Looka charges $72 for. You can download a logo "for free in industry-standard formats, including sharp SVGs, transparent PNGs, and fast-loading JPGs".


Its FAQ answers "Can others recreate my logo?" directly: "The design elements themselves (icons, fonts) are not exclusive to you and are available to all Wixel users." Icons and fonts are licensed for commercial use.


**Key features:**


- Free SVG, PNG and JPG downloads, with no paid plan needed.
- A brand theme that carries into your other Wixel designs.
- An AI tagline generator beside the logo editor.


**Pricing:** Free costs $0 with 120 AI credits a month and up to 20 logos, and paid plans add credits: Basic is $9 a month or $90 a year, Pro $29 or $290, and Max $59 or $590. Downloads in any format are included on every plan.


**Pros:** Free vector files, manual edits that don't use credits, yearly plans with two months free


**Cons:** Icons and fonts are shared with every Wixel user, AI generations and AI edits spend credits, you need a Wixel account


**The reason to try it:** It costs nothing to get an SVG, so you can test a direction before paying anyone.


**Final verdict:** Pick Wixel for a free vector logo, knowing its icon isn't yours alone.


### 7. LogoAI


**Overview:** LogoAI pitches itself as "a brand, not just a logo." Past the logo, it makes animations and brand videos, builds an AI brand kit, and runs a Design Studio with "20+ Top AI Models". The homepage lists SVG, PNG and PDF exports.


Its FAQ is direct about rights: "Paid LogoAI plans include commercial use of generated logos. Commercial use does not guarantee exclusivity or trademark registration." What happens to your access after you cancel is "subject to the terms shown for your plan".


**Key features:**


- Logo animations and short brand videos.
- An AI brand kit built around your logo.
- A Design Studio that switches between many AI models.


**Pricing:** A 7-day trial costs $10 with 200 AI credits, the Branding Suite and unrestricted downloads, then Pro renews at $20 a month with 500 credits. There's no one-time option and no free plan.


**Pros:** A $10 entry point, motion and video beyond the static logo, SVG and PDF exports


**Cons:** The trial renews at $20 a month unless you cancel within 7 days, some export formats and AI tools can use credits, access after canceling depends on your plan's terms


**When it beats Looka:** You want logo animations and brand videos on the same subscription as the logo.


**Final verdict:** Choose LogoAI if motion matters more to you than owning the icon.


### 8. LOGO.com


**Overview:** LOGO.com runs a free tier and monthly plans. Free is "Never billed" and gives you one logo with four high-resolution PNG files, while the Brand plan adds 42 vector files in SVG and AI formats, a brand kit, a done-for-you website and 1,200+ templates.


Its help center says the icon, font and basic shapes come from a curated library and "cannot be uniquely claimed or protected", and that "only the combined design as a whole may be eligible". It doesn't guarantee uniqueness. Files you downloaded on a paid plan stay yours after you cancel.


**Key features:**


- 42 SVG and Adobe Illustrator files on the Brand plan.
- A done-for-you website alongside the brand kit.
- Five seats and 2TB of storage on Business.


**Pricing:** Brand costs $15 a month, or $11.25 a month billed yearly, and Business is $50 a month, or $37.50 billed yearly. Enterprise starts at $500. A first Brand or Business purchase is refundable within 7 days, and an unused Brand renewal is refundable if you email within 7 days of the charge.


**Pros:** A free PNG tier, Illustrator files on the cheapest paid plan, downloaded files kept after canceling


**Cons:** Vector files need a paid plan, library elements are shared, no uniqueness guarantee


**Why it's here:** It packs 42 vector files into one $15 month, so you can download every layout you need and cancel.


**Final verdict:** Pick LOGO.com for SVG and Illustrator files on a cheap monthly plan.


### 9. Canva


**Overview:** Canva is a design suite with a logo maker inside, and its help center says plainly what a template logo can't do: "Canva's logo templates are customizable and can be used by anyone. This means that your rights to the logo are non-exclusive and you can't register it as a trademark."


The same page says stock graphics in a logo aren't suitable for a trademark, because "Elements in a logo need to be exclusive to you." Original artwork you upload, or a logo built only from fonts, simple lines and shapes, can be registered.


**Key features:**


- Logo templates you can edit in the same app as everything else.
- A Brand Kit, one on Free and five on Pro.
- Uploads of your own artwork, which Canva says you can trademark.


**Pricing:** Free costs nothing, and Pro costs one person $144 a year, or $18 monthly, with SVG export and transparent PNGs included. Business runs $250 per person a year.


**Pros:** A full design suite past the logo, a free plan, clear written guidance on trademarks


**Cons:** Template logos can't be registered as trademarks, SVG export needs Pro, no logo-specific package


**What Canva gets right:** It tells you up front which kinds of logo you can register, and why.


**Final verdict:** Use Canva to build a logo from fonts and simple shapes, or around artwork you upload, not to start from a template you plan to register.


### 10. Shopify Logo Maker


**Overview:** Shopify Logo Maker is the tool formerly called Hatchful. Its FAQ answers "Is Shopify Logo Maker free?" with "Yes, completely" and "No fees, no hidden paywall". You don't need an account to start, only an email address to receive the files.


The trade-off is in the files and the rights. You get "a high-resolution PNG, packaged in a zip file", with no vector version. Shopify also warns that "these logos are AI-generated, so similar designs could show up for other people" and suggests checking trademark availability first.


**Key features:**


- Free AI logo generation with regenerate and describe-a-change options.
- Mockup previews of the logo in use.
- Files emailed to you, plus an on-page download link.


**Pricing:** It's free, with no paid tier for the logo maker. The catch is the file format, since every logo comes as a PNG and no plan adds a vector version.


**Pros:** Free with no account, quick mockups, a candid warning about similar designs


**Cons:** PNG only, no brand kit, similar logos can show up for other people


**Best use for it:** A new store owner who needs a mark this week and will replace it before printing anything.


**Final verdict:** Use Shopify Logo Maker as a free placeholder, then move to a vector logo before your first print run.


## Who owns your logo: copyright, trademark and shared icons


Copyright and trademark protect different things. Looka gives you copyright in the finished logo, but its FAQ says stopping others from using it takes a trademark, and its help center says you'll "have to work with an outside attorney" for that.


Filing isn't free either. The[USPTO's fee page](https://www.uspto.gov/trademarks/basics/how-much-does-it-cost) says "the base application fee for each class of goods or services you include in your application is $350", so a filing in two classes costs $700 in base fees, before any attorney's fees.


Shared icons make that money harder to spend well. In an[r/graphic_design thread](https://www.reddit.com/r/graphic_design/comments/1how1lg/if_you_use_a_free_icon_as_a_logo_could_someone/) about stock icons in logos, one of the top replies described two local municipalities using the same stock icon, and a commenter who'd been through registration said approval "would be difficult" with similar marks already out there. It's anecdotal, but it matches what Looka, Wixel and LOGO.com say about their libraries.


Before you pay any of these vendors, check five things:


- The vendor's own sentence on whether its icons or templates go to other buyers.
- Whether exclusivity is included, sold as an upgrade, or never mentioned.
- Which file types the price includes, since printers ask for SVG, EPS or PDF.
- What happens to your files and edit rights when access or a subscription ends.
- Whether similar marks are already registered in your market.


If the first answer is "shared", you can still use the logo, but budget for a redesign before you spend $350 a class on a filing.


## Does what your logo shows affect sales?


Before you choose between an abstract symbol and one that shows what you sell, look at the research. Luffarelli, Mukesh and Mahmood studied logo descriptiveness, meaning how clearly a logo signals what a company sells. Across the 597 brands sampled in two of the six studies in their[Journal of Marketing Research paper](https://sussex.figshare.com/articles/journal_contribution/Let_the_logo_do_the_talking_the_influence_of_logo_descriptiveness_on_brand_equity/23483705) , 41% of logos were descriptive and 59% were not.


Descriptive logos were positively associated with sales across 423 listed consumer brands. In lab experiments, the boost to brand evaluations and purchase intentions was considerably weaker for familiar brands and reversed for categories people feel negatively about, so the case is strongest for a company people don't know yet.


That argues for a mark that shows your product. A logo is still one piece of a wider identity, and our explainer on[brand identity vs brand personality](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/brand-identity-vs-brand-personality) covers the rest of that system.

By that measure, Wixel is the cheapest vector logo you build yourself at $0, and Brandmark the cheapest you buy outright at $35. Design.com's few free template logos also include vector files. One month of LOGO.com at $15 or Design.com at about $25 also undercuts Brandmark if you cancel on time, since both let you keep your files. LogoAI's $10 trial is cheaper still, but it ties access after canceling to your plan's terms.


A contest or a designer costs more because you pay for someone's time, and if one contest feels too small, our[logo design agencies](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/logo-design-agencies) roundup shows what full agency projects run to.


## Generator or designer: how to choose


Start with how long the logo has to last. For a side project, a test store or next week's pitch deck, a generator is fine.


Once you plan to register the mark, the icon library becomes the problem, and the Looka competitors here split on it. Turbologo states exclusive rights, Design.com sells them on some logos, and Canva says you can register a logo built from its simple lines, shapes and fonts, or one you upload.


Budget sets the last boundary. A $249 contest suits a founder who wants options from people, and a design subscription suits a team that needs packaging, decks and ads in one style for years. Our take on[whether AI will replace designers](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/will-ai-replace-graphic-designers) covers where generators stop and designers still earn their fee.


## Looka competitors we left off


A few names from other roundups are left out on purpose. Tailor Brands still runs a logo maker, but its pricing page now sells LLC formation with no standalone logo price. DesignCrowd and BrandCrowd belong to the same group as Design.com, so one entry covers them.


Fiverr's logo maker blocked our checks, so we couldn't read its prices. Zoviz's Starter plan is $29 a month and its homepage advertises editable vector files, but we didn't read its exclusivity terms. To hand the whole brand to a firm instead, start with[finding a branding agency](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/the-ins-and-outs-of-finding-a-branding-agency) , which walks through that search.


## Which Looka alternative to start with


Need a free vector file today? Use Wixel. Want to own a cheap logo outright? Brandmark at $35 or Turbologo at $39.99 will do it, and Turbologo puts rights to the logo in writing, though its Terms don't guarantee uniqueness.


For a mark you plan to trademark, start with a person, whether that's a 99designs contest or a designer you hire. If you need the identity built and maintained, our[branding team on subscription](https://www.awesomic.com/branding) delivers a logo suite and brand book.


## FAQ


### Is Looka free?


Designing a logo on Looka is free, but downloading it isn't. The cheapest package is $35 once for a single 1000 by 1000 PNG on a colored background, and vector files start with the $72 Premium package.


### Do I own the logo I buy from Looka?


You own the copyright in the logo as a whole, not its individual elements. Looka's help center says it can't guarantee the copyright of icons and fonts, and it doesn't remove them from its database after you buy.


### Which Looka alternatives give you vector files for free?


Wixel is the one on this list that lets you download an SVG from its own AI logo maker on a free plan, though Design.com includes vector files on a few free template logos. LOGO.com's free plan and Shopify Logo Maker give PNG files only, and Canva puts SVG export on Pro at $18 a month.


### Can I trademark a logo made with a template?


Not from a Canva template: Canva says its template logos can't be registered, though original artwork you upload can be. LOGO.com says its shared icons and fonts can't be claimed, and only the combined design may be eligible.


### Can Looka build my website too?


Yes, on a paid tier. Brand Kit lets you build a site, but publishing it needs Brand Kit Web at $129 a year, the ecommerce version is $299 a year, and a custom domain costs extra. If the site matters more than the logo, our[Relume alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/relume-alternatives) roundup compares tools for planning and building one.
